newsitem.title: Singapore: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel steady, jet fuel firm.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel steady, jet fuel firm.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market was steady on Friday on perception that regional buyers were encouraged to buy at current low prices, while jet fuel continued to rise in a contango market, traders said.
But traders noted that an upswing in gas oil prices would be curbed by abundant supplies even as China was seen as a potential buyer at current values.

A European major, who has been a physical seller for most of this week on Friday sold a 150,000-barrel parcel of gas oil to a US major at $21.50 per barrel for July 5-9 lifting, free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
This was 10 cents lower than the European major's sale to a Chinese trader on Thursday.

Traders were now concerned that Indonesia's demand for July and August were limited to three million barrels per month, despite scheduled shutdowns at two refineries, as they were said to have sufficient gas oil stocks.
Initial estimates placed Indonesia's monthly requirements at more than four million barrels.
Taiwan has issued a tender to buy 0.3-percent sulphur gas oil for July 23-27 lifting, which closes on June 26.
The spot tender was in place of a scheduled term export tender for second half 1997 liftings, which has been deferred until after August because of current low regional prices.
Swaps gas oil for July gained 25 cents per barrel from Thursday, while August rose 15 cents on good buying support especially from a major.
The renewed confidence in the front month prompted the July/August time spread to narrow to minus 50 cents from minus 60 cents.

Jet fuel was discussed higher with two sellers--a Chinese trader and a European major--offering at $24.00 for the front and back end of July respectively. Bids came from a Singapore trader at $23.40 and $23.50 for early July and mid-July respectively, but nothing was traded.
Traders said jet fuel's strength was sustained by talk that Indonesia would take more than two million barrels in July, more than its normal one million barrels.
